content.intro: In this lesson, you will study cross-browser and cross-device testing and connect it to a small implementation or review task. The included subtopics preserve the attached Bootstrap curriculum outline.
content.why_it_matters: Cross-Browser and Cross-Device Testing makes the interface more robust for real users and real content. Measure and reproduce behavior, inspect semantics and focus, and document the browser, viewport, steps, and result so another developer can repeat the check.

content_blocks.text: Use the pinned Bootstrap 5.3.x baseline, follow the official component documentation, and verify semantic HTML, responsive behavior, and keyboard access before reusing the pattern.

content.task: Run a structured review centered on cross-browser and cross-device testing. Record reproducible steps, expected versus actual behavior, and one next fix or acceptance test.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the purpose and appropriate use of cross-browser and cross-device testing.

hints: Start with the smallest source example in this lesson.

content.expected_output: A working or reviewed example of cross-browser and cross-device testing, with a short explanation and recorded verification steps.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating cross-browser and cross-device testing as a visual-only change.
common_mistakes.why: A class or style does not automatically add semantic meaning, application logic, or secure server behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the appropriate HTML semantics and verify the actual interaction.

common_mistakes.problem: Checking only the default viewport or happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Responsive changes and interaction states can reveal issues that are not visible in a single screenshot.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat the task at a narrow and a wide viewport and include keyboard/error state checks where relevant.
